current.text: Dusty May is the new head coach.
It is unknown how May will split minutes among the centers Lively, Gafford, Powell and Johnson and forwards like Washington and Aldama.
Dereck Lively II, Dharma and Morez Johnson Jr. are all hurt.
Daniel Gafford is the likely opening night center.
Josh projects a starting five of Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, Cooper Flagg, P.J. Washington and Morez Johnson Jr.
The frontcourt is crowded with bigs and forwards, including Gafford, Lively, Washington, Aldama and Naji Marshall. Almost every player besides Kyrie Irving is a power forward.
The roster has 16 players and is overloaded with wings who expect minutes.
The deep frontcourt limits Santi Aldama's minutes.
The many power forwards limit Cooper Flagg's chances to block shots.
Dallas is short on ball handlers. The only real guards are Kyrie Irving, rookie Sergio de Larrea and Marcus Sasser. Christie and Flagg are not point guards.
Kyrie Irving is 36 and coming off an injury.
Cooper Flagg is the first priority on offense and Kyrie Irving is second.
Kyrie Irving's return will take shots mostly from players other than Flagg.
Dallas added shooting throughout the roster, including Santi Aldama and Sergio de Larrea.
Dallas is rebuilding on the fly around Cooper Flagg.
Dallas could be a bad team, but the weak Western Conference makes a playoff push possible. The win total of 34.5 points to a below-average team.
Dallas does not control its own pick. It is owed to Charlotte with top-two protection.
Dallas has no reason to tank and may push to win, so late-season shutdown risk is low.
Dallas has probably the best fantasy playoff schedule, 4-4-4 for 12 games, with only one back-to-back in those weeks.
Dallas has 16 back-to-backs, among the most in the league, which raises rest risk for its players during the regular season. It is the only high back-to-back team with a 4-4-4 playoff schedule.
Dallas plays only two games in the matchup week starting March 1, the last week before our playoffs.
One more move is expected, possibly a trade of Daniel Gafford and/or Klay Thompson.
Josh sees no strong fade on Dallas players and thinks most of their draft positions are reasonable.

durable.text: The front office cares little about positions and collects talent to see who sticks.

note: Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving carry the offense, and the 4-4-4 playoff schedule (12 games, best in the league) lifts every Dallas starter for weeks 19 to 21. With Lively and Morez Johnson Jr. hurt, Gafford gains early as the likely opening night center, but he is a trade candidate. The crowded frontcourt caps Aldama, Risacher and Flagg's blocks. Early on, watch how Dusty May splits the center minutes, Kyrie's health with 16 back-to-backs, and whether the expected trade happens. Remember the two-game week starting March 1, the last week before our playoffs.
